title: FCC bars Chinese robots and inverters already cleared for sale by Q2 2027
body: The Federal Communications Commission's measures of Tuesday, July 28 reach only forward. New Chinese humanoid and quadruped robot models, and new connected power inverters, cannot obtain equipment authorisation for the US market, but models already authorised for sale stay on it and deployed units keep running; the commission noted only that it retains the power to revoke those authorisations. That line is unstable because the stated rationale does not respect it. The security case is remote commandeering and data collection by devices sitting on American networks and grid infrastructure, and the precedent the commission cites is Volt Typhoon, the 2023 campaign that worked by seizing routers people had already bought and installed. A rule written against unreleased models does not touch the population that precedent is about. What changed on the same Tuesday is the cost of closing the gap. Counterpoint Research puts Unitree at just under a fifth of global humanoid market share and names Sungrow Power Supply and the already heavily sanctioned Huawei as inverter leaders, so reaching backwards would strand a real installed base. Against that, minority shareholder Humanoid Global disclosed that Agility Robotics has a definitive business combination agreement with Churchill Capital Corp XI at a 2.5 billion dollar pre-money equity value, with closing expected during 2026 and more than 620 million dollars of gross proceeds, alongside a 60,000-square-foot Fremont physical-AI development facility, roughly 200 added technical and field-operations roles, and more than 300 million dollars of multi-year Digit v5 orders subject to contractual milestones. A funded domestic substitute is what makes retroactive action affordable, and the politics already point that way: Representative John Moolenaar welcomed the action as strengthening domestic robotics, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned that Chinese AI firms could face sanctions over intellectual-property theft. The prediction is that the prospective-only line does not hold. By Q2 2027 the commission takes a formal step that reaches models already authorised for US sale in the categories the July 28 measures named: revoking at least one such authorisation, or issuing a further measure that subjects the already-cleared population to the same bar. Which instrument it uses is open; that the bar reaches backwards is the claim.

reasoning.because: The July 28 FCC bar covers only unreleased models; already-authorised Chinese units stay on sale
reasoning.given: The cited Volt Typhoon precedent is about already-deployed gear, and a funded US substitute exists
reasoning.so_that: The commission revokes existing authorisations or otherwise extends the bar to models already cleared for US sale
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; an FCC revocation or order naming already-authorised models
reasoning.plain_language: America just blocked new Chinese robots but let the ones already approved keep selling. That gap probably closes within a year.

summary: The FCC's July 28 bar on new Chinese robots and connected inverters leaves already-authorised models on sale. That carve-out sits badly with the commission's own Volt Typhoon reasoning, and a newly funded domestic alternative lowers the cost of closing it by Q2 2027.
